title: Arrest, Detention Home and the family's move to Louisville
summary: Neighbors shelter him, police take him to the hospital and the Detention Home; to get him out the family leaves town for Louisville.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: after that some people next door saw me get behind this box and they hollered, 'Hey, come over here,' after the boys passed. I jumped over the fence at some white people's house, they had known me, had me in their living room, they locked the door, I sat on a settee and I took the knife that I had and hid it in the pillows on the settee. They called the police, police came -- all the boys are gone now. So they got the police wagon out there, a Ford, what you call an open-top Ford, you know, four-seater. So they put me in the Ford, take me down to the station and I'm under arrest, naturally;but first they take me to the hospital where this boy was to recognize if I'm the fella. 'That's him,' says the boy. So the boy was being held by a policeman over there that's already in the hospital and the police got me so when he wants to get loose, I want to get loose 'cause we want to get together. It's all right with me. But he don't get away, I don't get away. They already know that's me because they've all recognized me -- that's me. Okay, I don't mind that's me.

So I go on with them to the Detention Home. They take me to the Detention Home, okay? I get to the Detention Home, they've got to notify my mother. But somebody notified my mother, the lady that had me in the house. She notified my mother and told her what had happened, told her the whole story. My mother come down to the Detention Home to get me and I had a reputation in that town. I mean a reputation. About the Indianapolis Star, about the Five and Ten Cents Store, Kinger's Packing House, all (inaudible).
Then? 12, 12 years old I think it was, 12 or 13.
However, the only way they could get me out of the Detention Home was to take me out of town and out of town I went. They put me into Louisville.
With your family, your whole family left?
Yeh, Yeh, they got to leave, they got to follow me.
